award_name: Alan Greenberg Bursary for Innovation in Entrepreneurship
award_description:
Alan Greenberg has a remarkable career by any standards, excelling in real estate development in North America and venture capital. Alan never accepts the status quo, but has always pushed himself and his teams to focus on how to be more efficient, to better serve customers, and to reduce waste of natural resources. A specific focus of Alan’s since the 90’s is to reduce real estate’s carbon footprint. He co-founded one of the world’s first Prop Tech venture capital funds in 2015 and then a second fund in 2020 that focuses on carbon reduction and social impact solutions for real estate. A well-rounded man, he also co-founded Your Music Memory, a world-class collection of unique, iconic rock ‘n’ roll memorabilia focusing on the art of the album cover. All the while, Alan’s strong belief in community has resulted in many philanthropic commitments, including devoting his time to serve on the boards of directors of hospitals, arts organizations, and other non-profits. Alan is a steadfast and loyal friend, his word is his bond, and you can count on him when he says he will help you. It is with deep gratitude for his unwavering support, advice, and friendship that his sister-in-law, Carla Cumming Sojonky, endows this award in his honor.

Awarded on the basis of demonstrated financial need and satisfactory academic achievement. Students must be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident. Preference given to Alberta residents. Students must submit an application to be considered for this award.

award_name: Alberta Athletic Award - Fall
award_description:
Applicant must:
- be a Canadian citizen, Permanent Resident or Protected Person (visa students are not eligible),
- be an Alberta resident, and to be considered an Alberta resident one of the following conditions must apply: – one parent, or legal guardian has maintained permanent residence in Canada for at least twelve (12) consecutive months immediately prior to commencing post-secondary studies and be residing in Alberta, or – Alberta is the last place the student has lived for twelve (12) consecutive months immediately prior to commencing post-secondary studies, or – the student was enrolled full-time at an Alberta public post-secondary institution for two consecutive terms during an academic year, or – the student?s spouse/partner has maintained permanent residence in Alberta for 12 consecutive months prior to the person attending post-secondary.
- be enrolled in the second or subsequent term of an undergraduate or professional program at a publicly-funded institution in Alberta in the current academic year.
- be enrolled in at least 60% of a full course load for the term. Institutions may determine what constitutes a full-time course load in each of its programs.
- be registered in the required course load in the fall 2019 and/or winter 2020 term. A term is defined as a study period of up to 17 weeks in length.
- have a minimum GPA of 2.0 on a 4.0 scale to be eligible for the award. Students in upgrading or college preparation programs may be eligible after completing one term of upgrading but are only eligible for the award for a maximum of one year, provided they meet the athletic requirements. Students must participate on a sport team designated by the Alberta College Athletic Conference ( ACAC ) or the Alberta University Athletic Association ( AUAC ). Apprenticeship students may be eligible after completing one period of an apprenticeship program. The student must show progress in their apprenticeship program.

award_name: Bill Ho Memorial Scholarship
award_description:
Bill emigrated from Hong Kong to Edmonton in 1976 as a Civil Engineer. He graduated in 1988 as a Respiratory Therapist from NAIT , working at the Royal Alexandra Hospital ( RAH ) until his untimely passing away in 2009 from gastric cancer. Bill was a loving husband and father. He was well respected and loved by all who knew him. At work, Bill’s patients always came first. He was a mentor to many respiratory students at the RAH . Bill had a calming effect at work, especially during critical situations. At Bill’s funeral, one of Bill’s co-workers stated, “You knew you were going to have a good shift, when working with Bill.”

award_name: Bruce & Kathy Macmillan Memorial Siviculture Scholarship
award_description:
This scholarship will be awarded in memory of Bruce Macmillan’s exemplary service of over 40 years within the forestry industry, including time as a program instructor at NAIT . The Bruce & Kathy Macmillan Silviculture Scholarship will seek to reward those who show dedication to achieving their full academic potential. An individual who receives this award will demonstrate the ability to strive for greater advancement and improvement in the field.
Available to second year students enrolled in the Forest Technology program at NAIT . Awarded on the basis of the most improved student. “Improvement” will be based on the greatest increase in weighted average between two first year courses (FORT1112 – Plant and Ecosite Identification and FORT1214 – Forest Soils and Plants) and two second year courses (FORT2314 – Reforestation, FORT2414 – Stand Improvement). Three to five candidates will be put forward to a panel of judges for scholarship selection. The judging is based on a rubric that will be provided to students. Students will be automatically considered for this award. No application is required.

award_name: Bruce and Lorraine Cumming Memorial Bursary in Animal Health Technology
award_description:
W. Bruce Cumming (1930-1993) was born and grew up on a small dairy farm in the Ottawa Valley. In 1952, his family moved to Edmonton, where he later met Lorraine Hargreaves (1931-2009). They married in 1957 and raised a family of five children in the Garneau community. Their compassion and generosity were reflected in numerous years of community and school volunteerism, as well as in the many and varied family pets over the years: cats, dogs, gerbils, turtles, guinea pigs, and even (once) a rooster! Their example of frugality, honesty, hard work, and generosity live on in the legacy they left: their children and grandchildren. This award is endowed in their honor by their daughter, Carla Cumming Sojonky, and the late Frank Sojonky.
Available to second-year students enrolled in the Animal Health Technology program. Awarded on the basis of demonstrated financial need and satisfactory academic achievement. Students must be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident. Preference given to Alberta residents. Students must apply for this award to be considered.

Raised on the very ground that was originally settled by his ancestors over a century ago in 1872, Carl was a man of the landâ€”always having a strong connection to the soil under his feet. A life-long learner, Carl was a red seal carpenter, a tower crane technician and was working to get his millwright ticket. A respected figure on jobsites, he was always generous with his advice, which, thanks to his countless hours in workshops and the books, he had in spades. Carl was a giving man who would quietly help people out, asking for nothing in return. This bursary, aiding students in need to complete their learning, is an extension of that nature. While he was taken away from us far too early, Carlâ€™s memory lives on with us and hopefully through those selected for this award.

award_name: Clarke Gould Occupational Health and Safety Memorial Award
award_description:
Clarke was born June 17, 1959 and was the eldest of 4 boys to Betty and Arthur Gould. Clarke was a loving father to three children. Clarke was passionate, funny, patient and kind. You could always count on Clarke, to tell a joke or one of his quick one-liners. However, when you remember Clarke the first thing that comes to your mind is his big heart! He cared so much about everyone around him and he would always lend a shoulder to cry on. His passion for helping others began at a young age where he became a life guard at the age of 16. Clarke became a leader within Scouts, an organization that offers youths an opportunity to experience new things, have more adventures and develop into confident and capable individuals better prepared for success in the world. This was who Clarke was, always giving to others.
Clarke graduated from the U of A with a degree in Economics with a minor in Gerontology, as he wanted to help the aging. Clarke worked for Atco Gas in their training department and moved from there to the family owned business, Gould Safety. He continued to work for Gould Safety as a trainer and health and safety professional for 30 years in all facets of safety and wrote programs and trained specifically for the Electrical contractors.
For approximately 20 years, Clarke was a member of the Alberta Construction Safety Association, Edmonton Regional Safety Committee. Clarke was a valued member of our committee, where he led many of our initiatives. Such as: NAOSH Week and the Provincial Skills Competition. Our committee benefited from Clarke’s enthusiasm and knowledge at every meeting.
Rest in Peace, our Friend, our colleague.
Available to students enrolled in the Occupational Health and Safety program. Awarded on the basis of volunteer work/community involvement. Preference will be given to a student whose volunteer work/community involvement is safety related/within the safety community.
Students must submit an application to be considered for this award.

Stephanie Katherine Wetz life has been full of challenges. At just four days old, she underwent open heart surgery and was diagnosed with a form of muscular dystrophy by time she was one. She needed to rely on a wheelchair from the age of 8. Through all that, Stephanie continued to persevere, obtaining her architectural technology diploma at the Northern Alberta Institute of Technology in Edmonton. The Executive Committee for CSC Edmonton Chapter is pleased to provide the Northern Alberta Institute of Technology with funds for this academic year in recognition of Stephanie Wertz.
Available to students enrolled in Architectural Technology and Interior Design Technology. Awarded on the basis of demonstrated financial need and satisfactory academic achievement.
Students must complete the application to be considered for this award.

award_name: Darcy & Sherry Grykuliak Bursary
award_description:
Darcy was born in Leduc, Alberta and spent most of his early life there. As a teenager he was raised with his sister by a single mother who worked as a bank teller with limited means. Darcy started working summers and after school part time in order to help his mother and save up money for his post secondary education. He subsequently attended and graduated from NAIT with a Civil Engineering Technology diploma, worked for five years as a technologist to pay off student loans and then returned to Lakehead University to obtain his degree in Civil Engineering.
Sherry was born in Humbolt Saskatchewan and lived as a child on a farm near the tiny village of Pilger. As a girl Sherry helped out on the farm with numerous chores as well as attending school. At the age of 17 Sherry came to Sparwood, BC and fell in love with the rivers and mountains. She left home and struck out on her own working various jobs. Sherry raised two boys on her own as a single mother making ends meet while providing her sons with a good life and lots of love.
In 2003 Darcy met Sherry in Cranbrook, BC. In 2004 they moved to Golden for Darcy to take on the Lead Engineer role on the Kicking Horse Canyon Highway Project where they spent 16 years when they moved back to Cranbrook. The Kicking Horse Canyon Highway Project was a big career opportunity for Darcy and Sherry supported Darcy in this move.
Darcy and Sherry know what it is like to live on limited means and are providing this bursary to provide students who are in similar circumstances an opportunity to further their education and have better futures. They have established funds to support their five grandchildrenâ€™s educational opportunities. They hope that recipients of this bursary will pass this kindness on to future generations when they have the means to do so.
Available to second year students in the Civil Engineering Technology program. Awarded on the basis of demonstrated financial need and academic standing. Selected recipients will be asked to submit a short description on what receiving the funds would mean to them, and how they might pay-it-forward later in their lives.
Students must complete the application to be considered for this award.

award_name: Darryl Mayan Bursary
award_description:
In his 64 years, Darryl Grant Mayan continually brought kindness and integrity to everything he did. He touched countless students’ lives while instructing at NAIT for nearly 35 years. He challenged his students to stretch and grow. He gave feedback with such care that students walked away smiling no matter what the outcome. Darryl will be fondly remembered as NAIT’s resident food critic in our dining rooms. It is hoped that his bursary will provide a struggling student with opportunity to pursue their dreams.

award_name: Dhariwal Family Bursary
award_description:
Mr. Amrik Singh Dhariwal and his wife Mrs. Sowaran Kaur Dhariwal were both adventurous, hardworking spirits always willing to help others in a selfless manner, throughout their lives. This award recognizes Amrik and Sowaran Dhariwal for their wonderful spirit of “caring for others” and for having passed on that spirit to their family.
Originally from India, Amrik moved to the UK in 1954 to start work, and the rest of the family joined him in 1959. Amrik and Sowaran worked hard 12 hours/day, six days a week often on split shifts (nights, days) so one parent could be home with the children Mave and Kewal. In the late 1970’s they moved to Canada, and became Canadian Citizens. During their lifetimes they helped hundreds of newly arrived immigrants get on their feet, often taking people they just met into their home. Amrik was a quiet, gentle-giant who never sought recognition and remembered fondly by all community and family members. Sowaran, the matriarch of the Dhariwal family, and a strong driving forces behind the success of the Dhariwal children was a leader and feminist of her time. She is also known for having a hobby of “match-making” and was instrumental in 39 couples being introduced, engaged and married.
Amrik and Sowaran continually encouraged their children to study and work hard as they always had. Amrik as a farmer who spent most of his life as a large scale Baker being promoted many times and Sowaran working for British Overseas Airways Corporation ( BOAC ) at a time when it was unheard of for women to work such industrial jobs. Consequently, both Mave and Kewal became lifelong learners, as did their wives Balwinder and Gurpreet. In 1980 Mave joined NAIT as an instructor in Mechanical Engineering and the following year persuaded Kewal to also join NAIT as an instructor in Computer Systems.
The entire Dhariwal family has supported the community by giving their time and money to various religious and cultural associations, professional societies, political organizations, coaching sports, volunteering, providing mentorship and fundraising for senior’s societies.
Available to students enrolled in a full-time credit program at NAIT . Awarded on the basis of satisfactory academic achievement, demonstrated financial need and to a student who demonstrates caring for others through volunteer activities, mentorship or giving back to the community. Preference may be given to an international student, newly immigrated student, or student athlete.
Students must complete the application to be considered for this award.

award_name: Donald Hildebrandt Memorial Scholarship
award_description:
Donald Hildebrandt graduated from the Forest and Resource Management program at NAIT in 1976. He worked as a Fisheries Technician/Biologist for Fish and Wildlife in Edson for 36 years and was well known for his wonderful sense of humor and his dedication to his work. As a biologist, Don returned to NAIT to engage students in fisheries field work, to talk to students about his career in fisheries and to share the finer details of fish aging techniques. Don was an inspiration to NAIT biology students who were just beginning careers in wildlife and fisheries; his contagious humor and enthusiasm encouraged students to pursue their dreams of working as technicians or biologists. Don passed away suddenly on March 28, 2015 at the age of 59 years.
Available to second year students of the Biological Sciences Technology – Conservation Biology program at NAIT . Awarded on the basis of academic achievement in the first year of the program and demonstrates enthusiasm and leadership in fish habitat restoration initiatives. Students will be automatically considered for this award. No application is required.

award_name: Dr. Dave Brace Award for Volunteerism in Animal Welfare
award_description:
A founding partner of the Bow River Veterinary Centre in Canmore, Alberta, Dr. Dave Brace became a local legend renowned for not only his exceptional skills and knowledge, but his remarkable kindness and compassion for both animals and their human companions. Dr. Dave is a founding board member of the Carla Cumming Sojonky Adoption Centre, Home of the Bow Valley SPCA , and volunteered many hours caring for rescued animals in Canada and the USA , most notably after Hurricane Katrina. This award is endowed by Carla Cumming Sojonky and the late Frank Sojonky in honor of the enormous impact Dr. Dave had on them, and their family of rescued German Shorthaired Pointers, in the Canmore community.
Available to second year students enrolled in the Veterinary Technology program at NAIT . Awarded on the basis of demonstrated financial need and satisfactory academic achievement. Students must be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident. Preference given to Alberta residents. Students must submit an application to be considered for this award.

award_name: Dr. Gary McPherson Leadership Scholarship
award_description:
Dr. Gary McPherson was an extraordinary Albertan who sought to improve the conditions and lives of people through his outstanding leadership ability. Despite being paralyzed due to polio, McPherson was a sports enthusiast throughout his life and helped to transform wheelchair sports into a worldwide sporting movement known as the Paralympics. McPherson was also a leader and advocate for the disabled community serving as Chair of the Premier’s Council on the Status of Persons with Disabilities and Vice-Chair of the Alberta Paraplegic Foundation. Gary received significant recognition and awards for his achievements including the prestigious Order of Canada, the Queen’s Jubilee Medal, the Alberta Order of Excellence, and both the Edmonton and Alberta Sports Halls of Fame. Above all, Gary dedicated his life to his family and to activities that promoted community development and support for young people. Gary passed away on Saturday, May 8, 2010.
An applicant must:
1) be a Canadian citizen, Permanent Resident or Protected Person.
2)Be an Alberta resident, and to be considered an Alberta Resident one of the following conditions must apply:
one parent, or legal guardian has maintained permanent residence in Canada for at least twelve consecutive months immediately prior to commencing post-secondary studies and be residing in Alberta
Alberta is the last place the student has lived for 12 consecutive months immediately prior to commencing post-secondary studies
the student’s spouse/partner has maintained permanent residence in Alberta for twelve consecutive months prior to the person attending post-secondary.
3) be enrolled full-time in a post-secondary program: undergraduate, professional, graduate, apprenticeship, diploma or certificate program at a publicly-funded institution in Alberta on the current academic year.
4) have shown outstanding leadership, especially in the area of disability, and/or initiative to improve the lives of other people while attending a publicly-funded post-secondary institution in Alberta.
5) be in satisfactory academic standing as determined by the post-secondary institution.
Students must complete the application to be considered for this award.

award_name: Forest Growth Organization of Western Canada - Brian Wesolowsky Memorial Prize
award_description:
Brian Wesolowsky, a graduate of the NAIT forestry program, was known throughout the Alberta Forest Industry as a field contractor with a passion for collecting accurate data and for innovations in tree measurement practices. He was instrumental in establishing and measuring plots that are part of major research projects managed by the Forest Growth Organization of Western Canada (FGrOW). After Brian’s unexpected passing in 2012, FGrOW members decided to honour his memory with the creation of the Brian Wesolowsky Memorial Scholarship. The scholarship is awarded annually to the student with the highest marks in the Forest Measurements course at NAIT .
Available to first-year students in the Forest Technology program. Awarded on the basis of top academic achievement in FORT1111, Forest Measurements. No application is required. Students will automatically be considered for this award.

award_name: Frances Camyre Memorial Bursary
award_description:
Frances Camyre was born in Maine in 1919, she grew up in Vancouver, where she worked as a hairdresser before moving to Moose Jaw with her husband, and then Whitehorse, where they operated a fleet of taxis and buses for tourists. After losing her husband in a fatal accident, Camyre returned to Vancouver to work in the hospitality industry and then moved back to Alberta to succeed in the oil and gas industry. Camyre partnered with two other oilfield veterans to establish Key Oilfield Supply & Rentals Ltd. in Calgary, a multi-million-dollar enterprise that provided equipment to the oil industry. She retired as CFO in 1987 and moved to New Westminster, B.C., where she lived until she passed away in 1992. Having missed the opportunity herself, Camyre focused on helping young people pursue a post-secondary education. Upon her death, she left $1 million to the Calgary Foundation to establish the Frances Camyre Memorial Foundation Fund, which awards bursaries to Alberta students based on scholastic standing, personal character, and financial need.
Available to students enrolled in any full-time certificate, diploma or degree program. Awarded on the basis of demonstrated financial need and satisfactory academic achievement. Preference will be given to Alberta residents.
Students must complete the application to be considered for this award.

award_name: Frank Sojonky Memorial Bursary in Alternative Energy Technology
award_description:
Born in Regina to hardworking Ukrainian immigrants, entrepreneur Frank Sojonky (1928-2012) grew up in humble circumstances during the Depression and war years. Through hard work, diligence, and drive, he was the first person in his family to graduate from university. Thereafter began a successful, 60-year career spanning many fields (from restaurants to real estate development) in Western Canada and beyond. He supported and fundraised for numerous charities, especially animal welfare and prostate cancer research, for which he raised millions of dollars. Through the ups and downs of business and his 23-year-fight against cancer, he maintained a remarkable attitude of optimism, innovation, and focus, and an unwavering belief in the power of an individual to make a positive contribution to the world. Together, he and Carla built an active, busy family of seven rescued German Shorthaired Pointers. This bursary is endowed in Frank’s honor by his beloved wife, Carla Cumming Sojonky.
Available to second-year students enrolled in the Alternative Energy Technology program. Awarded on the basis of demonstrated financial need and satisfactory academic achievement. Students must be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident. Preference given to Alberta residents.
Students must complete the application to be considered for this award.

award_name: GEARS Scholarship Foundation - Charles Hare Pioneer Bursary
award_description:
Charles Hare graduated from NAIT’s Mechanical-Industrial Engineering Technology program and became an ASET member in 1978. Shortly after joining, he took on leadership roles as Chair of the Red Deer Chapter and later served on ASET Council as Director, 2nd Vice President, and 1st Vice President. He went on to serve two terms as ASET President in 1987-88. His commitment to advancing the profession extended nationally through his work with the Canadian Council of Technicians and Technologists, where he served as President in 1997. During his ASET presidency in 1988, Charles played a pivotal role in establishing the Engineering Technology Scholarship Foundation of Alberta ( ETSFA ), later renamed the ASET Foundation. He remained an active contributor to the Foundation for decades, stepping down from the board in 2024 while continuing to serve as a voting member. Find out more about the GEARS Scholarship Foundation here: www.gearsfdn.ca.
Available to students enrolled in the following programs: Architectural Technology, Biomedical Engineering Technology, Building Automation Systems Technology, Laboratory Research and Biotechnology, Chemical Technology, Chemical Engineering Technology, Civil Engineering
Technology, Construction Engineering Technology, Electrical Engineering Technology, Electronics Engineering Technology, Engineering Design and Drafting Technology, Surveying and Geospatial Engineering Technology, Instrumentation Engineering Technology, Landscape Architectural Technology, Mechanical Engineering Technology, Petroleum Engineering Technology, Power Engineering Technology, and Water and Wastewater Technician. Awarded on the basis of demonstrated financial need and satisfactory academic achievement.
Students must submit an application to be considered for this award.

award_name: George & Sherry Elder Conservation Biology Bursary - Year 1
award_description:
George Elder was an instructor at NAIT from 1968-1972 in the Biological Sciences program. He was one of the founding instructors for this program and helped to create the relevant and practical training that focused on opportunities for employment in the Renewable Resources field that NAIT still values. During this tenure at NAIT , George worked summers in Banff which provided him the opportunity to work on the first Grizzly Bear Management program within the park under the direction of the Canadian Wildlife Service. This summer employment created opportunities to establish field trips in cooperation with the National Parks as part of the Renewable Resource Curriculum.
Available to first year students enrolled in the Biological Sciences – Conservation Biology program. Awarded on the basis of demonstrated financial need and satisfactory academic achievement in the first semester of the program.
Students must complete the application to be considered for this award.

award_name: Henri Daniel Memorial Bursary
award_description:
Henri Daniel was born in 1935 on a farm west of White Star, Saskatchewan. His career started with the Saskatchewan Department of Highways where Henri decided to further his education and become an electrician. While taking his apprenticeship he worked near Saskatoon and then moved to Dawson Creek, British Columbia where he found work with an electrical contractor. His work brought him to the Yukon, the W.A.C. Bennett Dam in Hudson BC and later to the South Peace School District. Henri spent the later years of his life calling Alberta home and living in northern and central Alberta until his passing in 2024. Henri was truly a very special, wonderful, kind and hardworking man. His nieces, Sonya and Selene, created this award in his honour, knowing he would be pleased to be a small part of studentsâ€™ academic journey in the Electrician Program at NAIT .

award_name: Indigenous Careers Award - Fall
award_description:
The Indigenous Careers Award is funded by the Government of Alberta and is intended to encourage Indigenous peoples (First Nations, Metis and Inuit) living in Alberta to pursue and complete post-secondary studies in certificate, diploma, applied degree and bachelor’s degree programs.
Available to NAIT students who are:
-Status Indian/First Nations, Non-Status Indian/First Nations, Metis, or Inuit and are able to provide a copy of proof of Indigenous ancestry (see below)
-Canadian Citizens, Permanent Residents, or Protected Persons of Canada
-Alberta residents
-Enrolled in the Fall semester in a certificate, diploma, applied degree, or bachelor’s degree program in at least 60% of a full course load (40% if you are a student with a documented, permanent disability)
-Achieving satisfactory academic standing
Selection will be based on demonstrated financial need.
Acceptable proof of identity may include:
1.) Certificate of Indian Status, a status card or a membership card
2.) Letter from their band verifying their status
3.) Membership card issued by a Metis organization the student is registered with (Metis organization must be a legal entity)
4.) A certified copy of a Nunavut Trust Certificate card or Inuit beneficiary card
5.) Letter of support from Indigenous and Northern Affairs Canada or Nunavut Tunngavik Incorporated
6.) A letter of support from a First Nation, Metis or Inuit organization (must be a legal entity) confirming the applicant’s indigenous ancestry
Students must submit an application to be considered for this award.

award_name: Jack Read Most Innovative Solution
award_description:
Jack Read was born on March 23, 1930, on the family homestead near St. Walburg, Saskatchewan and was nicknamed Jack after his brother Stewart’s imaginary friend. As a youngster, he worked on the family farms in Saskatchewan and later in Salmon Arm, BC. Jack loved building and fixing things. After a short post- WWII Navy service in Halifax, he settled in Edmonton where he transitioned from Typewriter Repairman to Automotive Mechanic and Service Station owner, to Oilfield Service Technician. In the 1980s, Jack started building and repairing oilpatch items, leading to the founding of Panama Enterprises (1990) Inc., initially working from home with his wife as a seamstress and eventually into larger facilities in West Edmonton. Jack became “Panama Jack”, known across the oilpatch for his signature Tilley hat and the outstanding windsocks among other products Panama Enterprises produced and delivered around the globe.

The Kevin Indergaard Respiratory Excellence Award has been established in memory of a valued NAIT staff member. Kevin was a graduate of the SAIT Respiratory Therapy program as well as obtaining a Bachelor of Education through the University of Alberta. He truly found his calling when he began his teaching career at NAIT . Kevin was a passionate educator as well as an excellent mentor and facilitator. Kevin held numerous roles at NAIT such as Program Head of the Respiratory Therapy program, Chair of Community Care Programs, Chair of Diagnostic imaging Programs, Associate Registrar and the Department of Teaching and Academic Development. He has always had a strong commitment to the field of Respiratory Therapy and was passionate about student professionalism and their commitment to quality patient care. He passed away suddenly and unexpectedly in 2013.

Awarded on the basis of professionalism, recognizable effort and continued improvement in clinical achievements, critical thinking and effective connection of theory with clinical applications, a high level of commitment to patient care and well-being and a commitment to inter-professional and community activities.
Students must submit an application to be considered for this award.

award_name: Metis Scholar Awards
award_description:
A student must be entering or continuing into a full-time certificate, diploma, applied undergraduate degree or undergraduate degree program in any school and must demonstrate a connection to the Metis Nation of Alberta.
Applications will be based upon the following criteria:
1. An applicant cannot be a current client of, or receiving funding from, any program at the Rupertsland Institute.
2. An applicant must show proof of Metis ancestry by submitting a copy of one of the following:
a.) A current citizenship card from the Metis Nation of Alberta; or,
b.) A current citizenship card from the Metis Nation of Alberta from a parent (along with the applicant’s long form birth
certificate) or from a grandparent (along with the applicant’s and the applicant’s parent’s long form birth certificate(s));
c.) A verifiable Metis citizenship application that is in progress with Metis Nation of Alberta Registry;
d.) A current citizenship card from one of the Metis National Council Governing members (Metis Nation British Columbia, Metis Nation-Saskatchewan, or Metis Nation of Ontario) or, the Manitoba Metis Federation.
3. The applicant must declare that his/her name will not appear on the Government of Canada’s Indian Registry, nor a Band list pursuant to the Indian Act, and is neither Inuk, nor non-Status Indian.
4. The applicant must declare that he/she is residing in the province of Alberta during their study period.
5. The applicant must declare all sources of student funding that that applicant is receiving including any financial support from a governing member of the Metis National Council, or Manitoba Metis Federation, or Alberta Metis Settlements.
6. An applicant must demonstrate current or recent involvement in the Metis community.
7. An applicant may supplement an application with information outlining the reasons for the chosen field of study, and how a Metis Scholar Award will impact the journey towards the completion of studies and career objectives.
8. An applicant who receives a Metis Scholar Award in one academic year may continue to apply for Metis Scholar Awards while continuing studies until graduation.
9. An applicant needs to know that priority will be given to Metis Nation of Alberta Citizens and those who have never received funding from Rupertsland Institute.
Students must also submit a letter outlining reasons for their chosen field of study, how a Metis Scholar Award will impact his/her journey towards education and career objectives. In addition, the letter should explain how they are involved in the Metis Community.
For additional information about the Metis Scholar Awards please visit http://www.rupertsland.org

award_name: Michael J. Burke Memorial Bursary in Millwork and Carpentry
award_description:
Born in Bathurst, NSW , Australia, Mike Burke (1940 – 2008) played professional rugby before completing a two-year training program and becoming a teacher at the age of 20; he later completed his education degree part-time. In 1967, he and his young family emigrated to Canada, settling in Edmonton. Mike and his wife Frances became teachers with Edmonton Public Schools, where he spent many years in various roles—-teacher, coach, assistant principal, and principal—-in junior and senior high schools. Mike’s easy-going nature, infectious sense of humor, and remarkable empathy made him a much-loved mentor to students and staff alike. He believed in second chances, hard work, and going the extra mile for others. At the time of his retirement, he had spent 45 years teaching in Australia and Canada. In his leisure time, Mike was a remarkable woodworker, building everything from remote-controlled yachts to carving delicate pieces of sculpture from exotic and native woods. His nativity scenes, Christmas ornaments, and stingrays were much-cherished gifts to family and friends. This award is endowed in Mike’s honor in recognition of his deep humanity and great friendship by Carla Cumming Sojonky and the late Frank Sojonky.
Available to first-year students enrolled in the Millwork and Carpentry program. Awarded on the basis of demonstrated financial need and satisfactory academic achievement. Students must be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident. Preference given to Alberta residents.
Students must complete the application to be considered for this award.

award_name: Micheal D. Laird Memorial Scholarship
award_description:
Michael D. Laird was a Red Seal Chef with a passion for Canadian cuisine. His culinary career took him across Alberta where he was inspired by Indigenous cultures and approaches to food and nature. Micheal’s menus reflected his unique, imaginative perspective on combining local ingredients (especially berries, which he recalled from his childhood on a farm) in new ways to create daring flavor profiles.
In Micheal’s memory, we have created the Micheal D. Laird Memorial Scholarship. Its purpose is to assist a student pursuing a career as a Red Seal Chef who shares Michael’s passion for farm-to-table cooking, and to raise awareness of mental health. The recipient must complete “Tough Enough to Talk About It” or similar mental health training. This award will help students build resiliency in dealing with the everyday demands of working in a high stress and high stakes environment.
Available to a student enrolled in the third period of the Cook apprenticeship program at NAIT . Awarded on the basis of academic achievement in the A18C0310 – Trade Math and Management course or the equivalent course containing menu planning curriculum. Recipients must have completed “Tough Enough to Talk About It” course, or other mental health resiliency training.
Students will automatically be considered for this opportunity.

award_description:
Recognizing both athletic and academic achievement, the Ooks Hockey Alumni Association Scholarships were created in 2003 to honor current Men’s Hockey players who exemplify the below attributes to their teammates. A minimum academic requirement of 1.7 (60%) in the case of extenuating circumstances, with a preference of at least 2.0 (63%) under normal circumstances is expected be achieved in the previous semester. Approximately 30 scholarships will be disbursed in two increments: one in February and one in May upon maintaining academic standing.
The Recipients are choses based on the following criteria:
A â€“ â€œATTITUDEâ€
A playerâ€™s attitude both on and off the ice. Positive attitude towards your teammates, coaches, school, program, and life in general.
L â€“ â€œLIKEABILITYâ€
A playerâ€™s likeability by the coaches, teammates, classmates and the Alumni. Generally a good person.
U â€“ â€œUNDERRATEDâ€
A player that may not have the most goals, assists and points at the end of the season. May not be the flashiest player on the team. However, a player that contributes just as much if not more to the benefit of the team based on his reputation and demeanor.
M â€“ â€œMOTIVATION TOWARD SCHOOLâ€
A player that demonstrates a good work ethic towards excelling in the classroom.
N â€“ â€œNAIT FOR LIFEâ€
A player who is not only committed to the current team and the school, but who will one day be committed to â€œGiving Backâ€ with a lifetime membership to the Ooks Hockey Alumni Association and contributing to the community. Award recipients are expected to be involved in the community through volunteerism.
I â€“ â€œINSPIRATIONâ€
A player that has become an inspiration to everyone around him â€“ through his attitude, likeability, underrated ability, work ethic in school, and his commitment to putting the team first.
Students will automatically be considered for this award. No application required.

award_name: Otto Bundschuh Memorial Bursary
award_description:
Otto Bundschuh worked as an instructor at NAIT for nearly 10 years, retiring in May 1991. Otto trained as an Auto Body apprentice and received his Journeyman status in the early 1950’s. He was part of the initial graduating Auto Body class that was provided at the Provincial Institute of Technology & Art located in Calgary, now called SAIT . Otto worked as an Auto Body Technician after graduation spending the majority of his career at Southpark Motors before joining NAIT . This award has been established in Otto’s memory by his family to support the next generation of Auto Body Technicians.
Available to students enrolled in the third period of the Auto Body Technician apprenticeship at NAIT . Awarded on the basis of demonstrated financial need. Apprentices must submit an application to be considered for this award. Apprentices will only be considered for the intake they attend NAIT .

award_name: R.J. Bailot Bursary for Volunteerism in Animal Health Technology
award_description:
R.J. Bailot is one of the founders of the Canadian Animal Task Force (formerly the Alberta Spay Neuter Task Force) and is currently the Executive Director of this non-profit. From an early age, R.J. was passionate about animal welfare and the people who live with and love their animals. His heroic work during the southern Alberta floods and the Fort McMurray wildfires saved the lives of countless animals. R.J. mentors many local and national animal welfare organizations; makes many presentations regarding the humane management of dog and cat populations on First Nations; is a compassionate and understanding expert on hoarding situations and the many complex issues hoarders face; and is very experienced with feral cats and managing this population. This award is endowed by Carla Cumming Sojonky and the late Frank Sojonky in honor of the enormous impact R.J. Bailot has made on the lives of countless people and animals.
Available to second-year students enrolled in the Veterinary Technology program. Awarded on the basis of demonstrated financial need and satisfactory academic achievement. Students must be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident. Preference given to Alberta residents. Students must submit an application to be considered for this award.

award_name: Ralph & Marlene Knight Bursary
award_description:
Ralph Knight graduated from the Electronics Engineering Technology program at NAIT in 1972. From 1972-1986 he gained experience in industry by working for several different employers. During this time he complemented his technology background with a four-year night course in Management Development from the University of Alberta. award_name: Shaun Yandt Clinical Excellence Award
award_description:
This award has been established in memory of a valued member of the Denturist program staff at NAIT . Shaun was a graduate of the NAIT Denturist class of 1981. He spent several years dedicated to his private practice but truly found his calling when he began his teaching career at NAIT in 1993. In his role as Clinical Director, he demonstrated a passion for clinical excellence. He passed away suddenly and unexpectedly in 2011.
Available to students enrolled in the third year of the Denturist Technology program at NAIT . Awarded on the basis of professionalism, recognizable effort and continued improvement in their clinical achievements, critical thinking and effective connection of theory with clinical applications, and a high level of commitment to patient care and well being.
Students will be automatically considered for this award. No application is required.

award_name: Sinclair Supply Ltd. Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Mechanic Bursary
award_description:
In 1947, Dan Sorochan started with Sinclair Supply Ltd. at the age of 19. Dan worked in various roles until he was promoted to General Manager in 1953. These bursaries were created to recognize Dan’s incredible lifetime commitment to the industry, Sinclair Supply Ltd., and his community. To celebrate Sinclair Supply Ltd.’s 75th anniversary, Sinclair Supply created an endowment to support these bursaries in perpetuity for the future generations of Sheet Metal, Gasfitter workers, and Refrigeration and Air Conditioning Mechanics.

Students must submit an application to be considered for this award. Students will only be considered during the period they were enrolled as a student.

award_name: TELUS Student Award
award_description:
At TELUS Friendly Future Foundation, our goal is to empower youth to build the skills, confidence, and sense of belonging they need to succeed today and in the future. To support young changemakers who are experiencing financial barriers and to accelerate access to post-secondary education, TELUS Friendly Future Foundation is entering its third year offering the TELUS Student Award program.
In keeping with our commitment to doing good in our communities and to bringing innovative ideas to life, recipients of the TELUS Student Award are encouraged to undertake a project or volunteering effort that will contribute to positive social, environmental or health outcomes in their communities.
For recipients who are committed to undertaking social impact efforts, we will be leveraging TELUS opportunities to add value and deepen impact, including offering Award recipients’ access to free mobile and discounted internet services (where available), mentoring, mental health services and other career development options.
Here are some examples of ways you can help contribute to positive social, environmental or health outcomes in your community:
- Lend a friendly hand: Volunteer with a local food bank, plant trees, organize a clothing drive for a shelter, or participate in other community service projects.
- Share your resilience: Volunteer as a mentor to help youth who can benefit from your skills, advice, and life experience.
- Build community: Mobilize fellow students for a shoreline clean-up or a charity walk or create an initiative solution to support isolated seniors.
- Spread the goodness: Support or launch an awareness campaign on social and environmental issues that affect the community.
Available to students enrolled in their first full-time diploma or degree program. Applicants must either be currently involved in or are planning on undertaking a social impact activity. Preference will be given to students who demonstrate financial need. Students must submit an application to be considered for this award.

award_name: The Arnold and Grace Rumbold Leadership Award
award_description:
Arnold and Grace have been steadfast champions of NAIT and its students for many years. Their commitment to education is reflected through their generous support of student awards, including the Arnold and Grace Leadership Awards. Through their philanthropy, they have demonstrated a deep passion for creating opportunities for underrepresented groups and helping students build meaningful careers. The Arnold and Grace Leadership Awards embody their belief in the transformative power of a polytechnic education and the positive impact NAIT students have in their communities
Available to full-time students enrolled in any year or period of a degree, diploma, certificate, or apprentice program who maintain satisfactory academic standing.

Community Impact – demonstrated volunteerism, service, or leadership that has made a meaningful difference on campus or in the broader community.
Applied Contribution – evidence of using practical, hands-on skills to solve problems, support others or improve community initiatives.
Leadership & Citizenship – showing initiative, collaboration, and responsibility in ways that inspire peers and strengthen community culture.
Students enrolled in a co-op program are eligible. However, activities completed as part of a co-op or other Work Integrated Learning experiences (e.g., clinical, field, or professional practice placements) will not be considered in the evaluation. Students may only receive the award once.
Students must submit an application and a letter of recommendation to be considered for this award.

award_name: The Four Directions Bursary
award_description:
The Four Directions Bursary is for Aboriginal (First Nation (Status and Non-Status), Metis, & Inuit) students who have been directly or indirectly impacted by the Canadian Indian Residential School system. This bursary is aligned with the Truth and Reconciliation Commission Calls to Action 10 and 11 to provide sufficient/adequate funding to Aboriginal students. NAIT is committed to supporting the full participation of Aboriginal peoples in higher education and removing barriers to Aboriginal student success.
The Four Directions Bursary is available to Aboriginal students in post-secondary degree, diploma and certificate programs, based on satisfactory academic achievement and demonstrated financial need. Applicants will need to provide a short written response outlining how this award will contribute to truth and reconciliation in post-secondary education and their personal post-secondary journey.
Students must complete the application to be considered for this award.

award_name: The Frank Bochek IT Bursary
award_description:
Frank Bochek is a retired electronics technician who was born and raised in the coal-mining town Sterco, in the foothills of Alberta. His innate curiosity and fascination of how things work make him the ultimate science guy, with a particular passion for computers and electronics. He was the owner/operator of Frank’s Radio Clinic in his early career, and was later responsible for small engine and electrical repairs as well as the installation and maintenance of computers in the Yellowhead School Division including the original Commodore 64. Throughout his life Frank has been committed to volunteerism and community work, cheerfully serving others.
Available to first year students enrolled in the Bachelor of Applied Information Systems Technology, Computer Engineering Technology, Computer Network Administrator, Electronics Engineering Technology, Network Engineering Technology and Wireless Systems Engineering Technology programs at NAIT . Awarded on the basis of demonstrated financial need as well as community involvement or volunteer work. Applicants must have achieved satisfactory academic achievement in the first semester of the program.
Students must complete the application to be considered for this award.

award_name: The Kamaljit Kaur Chungh “Legacy of Hope” Bursary
award_description:
In Loving Memory of Kamaljit Kaur Chungh
Ten years have passed since the world lost a soul of incomparable brilliance, yet the light Kamaljit Kaur Chungh ignited remains undimmed. A devoted wife, a dedicated CGA accountant, and a pillar of her family, Kamaljit defined what it meant to live with purpose and grace.
For nine years, she walked through the fire of cancer not as a victim, but as a warrior. While she faced a battle that would have broken many, she never once succumbed to self-pity. Instead, she chose to be a beacon of hope, radiating a warmth that guided everyone around her through their own dark times.
Kamaljit moved through life with a heart of pure gold and a beautiful, rare innocence. She possessed a soul so kind that she truly could not see the evil in the world, choosing instead to believe in the inherent goodness
of every person she met. She was a fierce advocate for the power of education and lived by a simple, profound creed: to help others and to be the very best human being one could possibly be.
Though she took her final breaths surrounded by the family who adored her, her journey did not end there. A decade later, her impact continues to ripple through the countless lives she touched. Kamaljit remainsâ€”now
and alwaysâ€”deeply loved, profoundly missed, and forever admired for the light she brought into this world.
Available to students enrolled in the Business Administration – Accounting program. Awarded on the basis of demonstrated financial need and satisfactory academic achievement in the previous semester of the program.
Students must submit an application to be considered for this award.

award_name: Trevor Hepburn Edwards Scholarship III - Architectural Technology
award_description:
Trevor Hepburn Edwards (1944 – 1994) was a Canadian Architect, registered in the province of Alberta. Never one to find the easiest way, Trevor came to his vocation and career over a considerable length of time. He knew in high school that he wanted to be an Architect, but quickly learned that high school grades and personality would only take him so far. This occasioned a rethinking of his goals and aspirations, and, following a series of false short-cuts, he ultimately achieved his Architectural Technology Diploma at NAIT , and then pursued a University degree and accreditation, and became an influential Architect within the public sector. Trevor believed fervently in the importance of lifelong learning, and intended to create scholarships that encourage mature, working adults to return to full-time education at the post-secondary level, in diploma or degree programs, that may lead to successful careers. This scholarship is intended to fulfill Trevor’s stipulations by finding and rewarding these specific students.
This scholarship is available to a student in the Architectural Technology program. It will be awarded on the basis of a minimum GPA of 2.0 and a one-page essay submission. The essay should provide a brief summary of the applicants work history to date, and clearly articulate the applicants ambition and passion to pursue a higher education to achieve career goals and successes in life, demonstrating the characteristics that Trevor wished to encourage. Previous recipients are not eligible to reapply. Applicants must be a Canadian citizen or Permanent resident. Preference will be given to a mature student who is returning to school after having been in the workforce for five or more years. Students must complete the application to be considered for this award.

award_description:

Awarded on the basis of costs incurred to cover the cost of materials, books, and supplies required for technical training while at NAIT . Students will be required to submit proof of expenses in the form of itemized receipts.

- Textbooks
- Other required learning materials identified by the program
